method: Second pass on 2026-10-12 with direct page access. Every source that could be read was re-read: excerpts are verbatim page text, confirmed mechanically on the page, and every claim was judged by an independent verifier (supported, correctly encoded, correct agreement). Sources behind bot protection could not be read and are kept unchanged from the first pass (2026-10-11, domain-restricted web searches), marked retrieval web_search. Publication years come from page metadata or visible dates (last-modified year for continuously edited pages); null when the page has none.

anchor-point.notes: Ten sources from seven publishers: Surf-Forecast, Wikipedia, Surfertoday (403, kept from the search pass), WannaSurf, Surf Atlas (four pages, one publisher), Stormrider and WSL. Wind dispute: only Surf-Forecast supports the profile's NE (45). WannaSurf gives SE-E (112), Surf Atlas's season guide gives E-SE (112), and Surf Atlas's Morocco page says east (90, the 45-deg edge). The direct evidence leans east, not northeast, so the profile's 45 deserves review. Tide: no source supports the profile's mid. Surf-Forecast says low; WannaSurf and Surfertoday say all tides. On a small WSL contest day in 2023 the waves broke at low tide and stopped as the tide rose (an observation, not recorded as a value). Size: WannaSurf 3 to 16+ ft, Surfertoday 3-15 ft, Surf Atlas up to 10-12 ft and '2-3 m without issue'; the profile's 3-12 ft fits the core, but two sources say it holds more. Swell direction: NW everywhere; WannaSurf adds N and Surf Atlas adds W. Season: November to April (Surf Atlas), September to April for the area (Wikipedia), summer mostly flat (Surf-Forecast); October is the weakest-supported profile month. Period: only qualitative (groundswell, long period); no numbers. Bottom conflict: sand (Surf Atlas Taghazout), sand with rock (WannaSurf), sand and reef (Surfertoday), a rock thumb point (Surf Atlas guide). Ride length conflict: 300-500 m (WannaSurf, Surfertoday), over 1 km (Stormrider), about 2 km linked with Hash Point (Wikipedia). Gaps: no official Moroccan or peer-reviewed source on conditions. Crossref found only Taghazout tourism-geography (Via Tourism Review 2014, read: no spot conditions), seawater-quality and shoreline-change papers.

bells-beach.notes: Seven publishers. Wikipedia, Surf-Forecast (Rincon and Bowl pages), WSL (two posts), SURFER (Surf Spot Mechanics, 2026, republished on Yahoo), SLS Beachsafe and Yeeew were read directly. Surfer Today (403) is kept as web_search. Biggest gain: SURFER's 2026 Surf Spot Mechanics piece. It gives an ideal swell direction of 196-215 deg (window 196-224) and a period of 15-16 s or longer, the first numeric period for Bells. It also gives a straight-offshore NW wind, with W-NW ideal and N-NE a 'devil wind'; a head-high to triple-overhead size; an April-September storm season; and an offshore ridge that refracts swell onto a gradually rising rock reef. Wind: NW from Surf-Forecast (two pages) and SURFER, all 15 deg from the profile's 300. Tide depends on the section. Surf-Forecast's templated line says mid on the rise (consistent with low_to_mid). SURFER says low for the Bowl and high for Rincon. Surfer Today (search evidence) says almost any tide. The profile's low_to_mid fits the Bowl. Size: Anderson's 3-4 to 10-12 ft Bowl (scale not stated), SURFER's head high to triple overhead and Yeeew's 'classic at six to eight foot (double to triple overhead)' are roughly consistent with 3-15. Yeeew's own conversion shows that local Victorian feet are about half the face height. SLS Beachsafe says it handles 1.5-7 m (up to about 23 ft), above the profile's maximum. Season: April-September (SURFER), April (WSL), March-October (Surfer Today), summer flat (Surf-Forecast); all consistent with March-September. Not found: a peer-reviewed reef study or an official wave description. The Bells Beach Coastal and Marine Management Plan PDF on marineandcoasts.vic.gov.au returned 403. The Surf Coast Shire PDFs and the Bells Wikipedia article say nothing about the waves. The Victorian Heritage Database link did not respond. WannaSurf's Australia index pages returned empty, so no WannaSurf Bells page was reached. Source type: SLS Beachsafe is run by Surf Life Saving Australia, a national lifesaving organisation, not a government agency, so it is classed community here. Its beach texts read like a coastal beach inventory; the project lead may want to reclassify it.

bocas-del-toro.notes: All 6 sources were read directly (5 publishers: Surf-Forecast, WannaSurf, The Inertia, Sol Bungalows, Club Venao). None is encyclopedia, official or peer-reviewed. No Wikipedia article covers the break; the Bastimentos Island article only mentions the island's August-March wave season. Crossref was not searched (no plausible break study). Swell direction: Surf-Forecast NE, WannaSurf N-NE and Club Venao NE all sit inside the 350-40 optimum. Wind: Surf-Forecast says SW is best and offshore; WannaSurf lists SW/S as good wind. Both are within 35 deg of 190. Club Venao's 'Wind: SW' does not say offshore or best, so it has no value. Turko (The Inertia) says offshores funnel down the channel between the islands and chop up the face, which is a local wind effect. Size: WannaSurf says it works from 5-6 ft and holds 16 ft and over; Club Venao says it 'can hold over 20ft'. That phrasing mirrors Magicseaweed's description (quoted on a 2017 blog), so it may not be independent. A WannaSurf contributor says it only breaks once Dumpers is over 8 ft. Period: nothing numeric; Surf-Forecast says windswell is more common than groundswell. The 9/12 s profile values are unsupported. Tide: Surf-Forecast, WannaSurf and Club Venao all say all tides. The profile's null could become 'all'. Season: Turko gives Nov-Apr and Sol Bungalows Dec-Apr, both for Bocas generally. Club Venao gives Jan, Feb and July, but the same line appears for every Bocas spot on its page (templated). Surf-Forecast's March/spring line is only in the raw HTML widget and was dropped. July is outside the profile's Dec-Mar; Sol Bungalows also calls June-August a secondary 'mini season' for Bocas. Bathymetry: coral reef and sharp rock, breaking in deep water over a cavernous reef (WannaSurf). Sol Bungalows calls it a deep-water slab. No measured bathymetry exists. Turko also says the swell faded 'once the tide started sucking out'. This was not recorded as a tide preference because it describes one session.

burleigh-heads.notes: Read directly: Surf-Forecast, WannaSurf, WSL x2, Surf Atlas, National Surfing Reserves, Experience Gold Coast, City of Gold Coast, Wikipedia (Burleigh Heads suburb page, which has only a short surfing note). Could not read: SurferToday (403), mondo.surf and surfnerd (403, found by search). WIND: Surf-Forecast's SW offshore matches the profile. Surf Atlas's winter southerly offshores sit at the 45 deg boundary. WSL says northerlies are the dreaded wind. WannaSurf's NW/W is the outlier. SWELL DIRECTION: SSE (Surf-Forecast), SE (WannaSurf), SE-S (Surf Atlas); readable sources lean slightly south of the profile optimum max of 150, so consider ~100-165. TIDE is in conflict: Surf-Forecast and WannaSurf say all tides (WannaSurf prefers rising). Experience Gold Coast says a rising mid tide is safer but the lower tide gives racetrack sections, which supports low_to_mid; SurferToday's 'lower tides' is unreadable. Surfing Reserves notes the Cove's rocks are exposed at low tide. SIZE: WannaSurf starts at 5-6 ft and holds 10 ft+, and WSL says it handles sizable swell better than nearby spots. The profile's 3-12 ft is broadly consistent, though WannaSurf's minimum is 5 ft. PERIOD: no seconds; Surf-Forecast says a mix of groundswell and windswell. SEASON: Surf-Forecast and Surf Atlas both say winter (Jun-Aug), which conflicts with the profile's Jan-Jun emphasis. Only SurferToday (unreadable) gives Dec-Mar, and WSL notes the January event often meets summer flat spells. BATHYMETRY: a sand-over-rock point (WannaSurf, Surfing Reserves, WSL 'sandbar'). Tallebudgera Creek feeds shifting banks (Surf Atlas). WannaSurf dates beach bulldozing to 1999-2000. chicama.notes: Wind is now a two-sided conflict. East/east-northeast as offshore or best: Surf-Forecast ENE, WannaSurf E/NE, LatAm Surfing E, MyWaveFinder E; all 60-82 deg from the profile's 150. Southeast as best: Chicama Surf Trips (local operator, 2024) and Surf Escape (2023); both 15 deg from 150. Wikipedia and a WannaSurf user comment say only that the wind is (predominantly) offshore. Surfing-Waves says the prevailing winds are south/southwest. So no direct source supports SSE (150) exactly. The weight of descriptive sources leans E. A value of about 90-135 would fit more of them than 150. Swell size: Wikipedia (the only source that converts its scale) says the main point holds at least 10 ft Hawaiian, about 20 ft faces, above the profile max of 12. Several guides put the best range at 4-7 ft (scale not stated). Period: the only numeric source is Topologica (14-18 s). It is undated, of unknown authorship and possibly machine-generated, so treat it as low weight. Other sources say only long-period groundswell. Tide: WannaSurf, MyWaveFinder and Surf Escape say all tides, matching the profile. Topologica says mid-incoming to high to connect the sections, and Surfer Today (unread) said low to mid. Season: March/April-October/November across eight publishers, consistent with the profile's March-October. NASA Earth Observatory is classed official (a US government Earth-science agency; its text quotes a University of Maine oceanographer). No peer-reviewed study or measured bathymetry of the Chicama wave was found (Crossref returned only fisheries, archaeology and 1960s water-temperature papers for Puerto Chicama). A Spanish-language search for thesis or modelling work found nothing specific.

cloud-9.notes: 9 sources: 8 read directly, plus SurferToday kept unchanged as web_search (403). 7 publishers. Wind is well supported: Wikipedia (SW monsoon offshore, island-wide), Surf-Forecast (SW best/offshore), Fat Lips (best wind SW) and Strike Mission's profile (SW, 180-270 offshore range). All are 35 deg from the profile's 260, within tolerance, but they centre on 225; consider moving offshore_wind_direction toward 225-240. Swell direction: Surf-Forecast, Fat Lips and Siargao Local say NE (45); Strike Mission's profile says NE 20-90. Every source puts the best direction about 15 deg north of the profile's 60-110 optimum, so consider widening optimal_min to about 45. Size: Fat Lips gives a best range of 2-10 ft, which matches the 10 ft max (the min is 2, not 3). The WSL contest reports (2018, 2024) saw excellent 4-6 ft days. Period: only Strike Mission's 14 s reference (a model input, community) gives a number; the 9/13 s profile values are otherwise unsupported. Tide: Surf-Forecast high and rising, Fat Lips mid-high, Siargao Local mid-to-high, Strike Mission mid-to-high, In Siargao mid. A WSL report saw fewer barrels as the tide dropped. All support mid_to_high. Season: Wikipedia Aug-Dec (island-wide), Fat Lips late Aug-Nov, Siargao Local and In Siargao Aug-Nov, Strike Mission Aug-Nov. These match the profile's Aug-Nov. Surf-Forecast's guide text says autumn and winter, while its raw-HTML season widget says summer/September, an internal inconsistency. Strike Mission calls Aug-Nov the 'NE monsoon', but in the Philippines Aug-Nov is the SW (habagat) monsoon, which points to generated text. Its values are a scoring profile labelled 'community' data. Siargao Local and In Siargao are 2026 web guides of unknown authorship. Fat Lips is a local surf school (undated). No peer-reviewed or Philippine government source about the break was found; Crossref returned only general reef-hydrodynamics and tourism papers. Bathymetry remains unmeasured: the evidence is Wikipedia's Philippine Trench statement and SurferToday (unread).

cloudbreak.notes: Ten sources from ten publishers; nine were read directly. Surfer Today (403) is kept unchanged as web_search. Wind: Yeeew says the best wind is SE (135). Perfect Wave Travel says Cloudbreak is straight offshore in the trade winds and gives the Mamanuca trades as ESE (112.5). This is indirect: it is a comparison with Frigates Pass, and the direction comes from another entry on the page. Both agree with the profile's 135. WSL's 2015 table lists 'Wind: E, ESE, SE 5-15kts'. The table does not say offshore or best, so it is now recorded as a wind window with no offshore value. The window includes SE. Surf-Forecast contradicts itself on one page: its summary says the best wind is SW, and its conditions line says ENE offshore. Both are recorded with agrees false and look like templated text. Tide is still split. WSL's table says Low and Tourism Fiji says 'All, but best between low and mid'; both are narrower than the profile's 'all'. Yeeew says all tides (agrees). WSL's own local surfer warns to stay away from the inside at low tide. Size: WSL, Tourism Fiji and the Tavarua resort give 2-20 ft. A local surfer in the WSL piece says it holds 25-30 ft. WannaSurf's minimum is 5-6 ft. Perfect Wave Travel says it is fun at 3 ft and serious at 6 ft, which is not a range. Swell direction: six publishers give SW, S-SW, SSW or 210-240, consistent with 200-235. Period: only WSL gives a number (16 s+). New peer-reviewed source: Scientific Reports (2025). It mapped the Cloudbreak reef with structure-from-motion photogrammetry (a measured DEM) and GPS surfer tracks, and cites a typical incident direction of 210-240 deg. It reports zone-level slope and complexity, not depths. Source types: Tourism Fiji is a tourism board, so magazine under v1.2. The Tavarua resort and Perfect Wave Travel (tour operator) are community. The WSL post is magazine.

coxos.notes: Four publishers: Surf-Forecast, WannaSurf, Surf Atlas and Stormrider (region page). Wind: SE offshore (Surf-Forecast, 25 deg from the profile's 110) and a SE-E-NE window (WannaSurf) both agree; no source names a single easterly offshore exactly. Swell direction: NNW (Surf-Forecast), N-NW (Surf Atlas) and NW-W-SW (WannaSurf) all overlap the profile's 300-330 optimum; the evidence leans more northerly than the profile, and WannaSurf's SW is outside the window. Size: only WannaSurf (5 to 16 ft or more), consistent with the profile's 4-15 ft. Tide: WannaSurf low to mid (overlaps the profile's mid); Stormrider warns that some Ericeira ledges get dangerous at low tide (region-wide, not recorded). Season: Surf Atlas November-March for the northern reefs; Stormrider says autumn for Ericeira as a whole; Surf-Forecast says it can work any time of year. Gaps: no swell period figure from any source; no peer-reviewed or official source on Coxos. Crossref found two Ericeira World Surfing Reserve wave-modelling papers (ICCE 2025, OMAE 2024); the readable ICCE extended abstract does not mention Coxos, so nothing was recorded.

desert-point.notes: Wind conflict now leans clearly to the profile: four readable sources give southeast (135 deg) as the best or offshore wind (WannaSurf, Indonesian Surf Guide, LMBK Surf House); only Surf-Forecast's template says east-northeast (67.5 deg). Swell direction: SW (Surf-Forecast, WannaSurf, Indonesian Surf Guide, DHM) and S-SW (LMBK), all near the profile's 205-235 optimum. Size: WannaSurf starts at 5-6 ft and holds 8 ft+, Indonesian Surf Guide gives head high to double overhead (about 6-12 ft faces), DHM gives 4-6 ft Hawaiian as optimal (about 8-12 ft faces); the profile's 12 ft maximum is now supported, but its 4 ft minimum is below every source's starting size (5-6 ft). Period: LMBK says swells under 14 s struggle to wrap into the bay, which supports the profile's 14 s minimum; nothing supports the 17 s ideal. Tide is still split: low tide (WannaSurf 'Low tide only', rising; Indonesian Surf Guide 'best at low tide') versus mid-incoming (DHM: 'dangerously shallow at low tide and closes out at high tide'); WannaSurf's own text also warns 'Watch out for low tide sessions!!'. The profile's low_to_mid covers both readings. Season: May-September (LMBK, DHM) or May-October (Surf-Forecast, Indonesian Surf Guide). Consistency conflict: Surf-Forecast's template says 'quite reliable surf' while WannaSurf, Indonesian Surf Guide, LMBK and The Inertia call it fickle or inconsistent. Independence caveat: the new sources are mostly surf-camp or directory sites, and Indonesian Surf Guide's page promotes LMBK Surf House. Dated sources: The Inertia 2023, indonesia.travel 2025, Indonesian Surf Guide 2025, LMBK 2026, DHM 2026; Surf-Forecast and WannaSurf are undated. Surfer Today still returns 403 and is kept from search evidence. No peer-reviewed, survey or official source was found (Crossref searches returned nothing on this break).

dungeons.notes: Eleven sources from eight publishers; nine were read directly. The two Surfer Today pages returned 403 (Cloudflare) and are kept unchanged as web_search. No peer-reviewed, official or survey source was found; Crossref returned nothing for Dungeons or Hout Bay. Wind: N-centred winds agree with the profile's 30. WannaSurf (both entries) gives N/NW/NE, Yeeew N, and Surfer Today N or NW-NE. Surf-Forecast's NW (315) contradicts. surfing.world, an unattributed and possibly machine-written blog, says a light SE wind is best; this is a weak outlier. Stormrider's Dungeons page holds 'Northerly' wind, 'Low to Mid tide', S-W swell and 10-30+ ft. Those values are only in the page's script data and were not recorded. Tide: low or low-to-mid from Surf-Forecast, Yeeew and Surfer Today agrees. WannaSurf's main entry says all tides. The Slab section prefers mid to high and gets super shallow at lower tides; that is section-specific and not compared. Size: WannaSurf's minimum is 12 ft (Slab 6 ft), Yeeew's is triple overhead (about 18 ft), and Surfing-Waves says it only works on big swells. Both record waves (47 ft swell and the 65 ft Greg Long ride) were dropped. Period: only Surfer Today (unreadable) gives 15-19 s. A Ticket to Ride camp blog says Cape Town rarely gets periods over 15 s, which suggests the profile's 17 s ideal is uncommon. Bathymetry: the reef depths (2.5 m and 3.5 m) come from Wikipedia, not a hydrographic survey. Stormrider's Cape Peninsula region page only names Dungeons as a big-wave venue and was not recorded. Unreachable: surfsisters.co.za (no response) and brandsouthafrica.com (404). Seasonality: winter, from Jun-Aug up to Apr-Sep; it agrees.

g-land.notes: Wind agrees with the profile (120 deg): southeast trades (Wikipedia, WSL 2022 preview, World Surfaris) and east (Surf-Forecast, Surf Indonesia); Indonesian Surf Guide's E-NE (67.5 deg) is the only outlier. Tide is still the main conflict and leans away from low_to_mid: high (Wikipedia 'bigger and better at high tide'; World Surfaris for swells of 8 ft+ and for Speedies), mid to high (Indonesian Surf Guide), mid (Surf-Forecast), all tides (Surf Indonesia); only World Surfaris' personal tip ('surf Money Trees on low tide') supports low, and Wikipedia says barrels get more critical as the tide drops and low tide at Speedies can be very dangerous. Size: Wikipedia gives Moneytrees as 2-10 ft Hawaiian (about 4-20 ft faces) and Indonesian Surf Guide head high to triple overhead+, so the profile's 15 ft maximum looks low; its 4 ft minimum matches Wikipedia. Period: Indonesian Surf Guide 14-18 s (and Surfer Today, unread, about 14 s), consistent with the profile's 13 s minimum and 16 s ideal. Swell direction: SW (Surf-Forecast, Surf Indonesia) and S-SW (WSL 2022, Indonesian Surf Guide), inside the profile window. Reef length conflict: Wikipedia half a kilometre (rideable point over 1 km), WSL 1.5 km. Season: April-September (Wikipedia), April-October (Surf Indonesia), May-October (Surf-Forecast, Indonesian Surf Guide), all consistent with the profile. The earlier WSL claims were on the 2022 preview, not post 453801 (now magazine type, with only the section description). Both ResearchGate items return 403 and are kept from search evidence; Crossref shows the Plengkung marketing paper (Jurnal Kebijakan Pembangunan, 2021, DOI 10.47441/jkp.v16i2.201), but its abstract does not contain the April-October claim and the journal PDF timed out. No surf-break or bathymetry study and no Alas Purwo National Park page with conditions were found.

jaws-peahi.notes: All 7 readable current sources were re-read and 2 new ones added: Yeeew and Hawaii Life. WIND: readable sources agree on a southerly offshore: Surf-Forecast SSW, WSL BWT guide calm winds from the south, WannaSurf S and Yeeew S. The only contradiction is Surfertoday's E-SE (403, unchanged). Several WSL pages note that strong trades are the usual problem. SWELL DIRECTION CONFLICT: WSL (Surfline text) says the window opens about 305 and 320+ is best, so the profile window min of 290 may be too wide. WannaSurf, Yeeew and Hawaii Life say N, within 15 deg of the 315-345 optimum. Surf-Forecast's NNE (22.5) is outside the optimum and recorded as contradicting. WSL says westerly sets barrel. SIZE: 60+ ft faces (Wikipedia, WSL x2). Yeeew says good from triple overhead (about 18 ft faces, converted). WannaSurf says over 12 ft, scale unstated, not compared. WSL says the reef handles any size. PERIOD: still only qualitative (groundswell). No readable source gives seconds; buoy readings in event stories (Flux Hawaii) were not recorded. TIDE: 'all' from Surf-Forecast, WannaSurf and Yeeew. BATHYMETRY: WSL trench 100->20 ft, WSL underwater ridge NW of Maui, Wikipedia underwater ridge studied by scientists. The Fearing & Dalrymple Univ. of Delaware refraction study could not be reached and the USGS WRI 2000-4046 Maui bathymetry has no abstract. Not readable (403): Surfertoday, ResearchGate, mondo.surf.

jeffreys-bay.notes: Seven readable sources from seven publishers: Surf-Forecast, Wikipedia, WSL, WannaSurf, Stormrider Surf Guides, Yeeew and Surf Atlas. No peer-reviewed or official source was found; Crossref returned nothing for J-Bay surf or Supertubes. WIND CONFLICT, still the main issue. The best or offshore winds given are: WSL best-conditions table SW/WSW (236), WannaSurf SW (225), Yeeew SW/S (202.5) and Surf-Forecast WSW (247.5). Only Surf-Forecast's WSW is within 45 deg of the profile's 290. Surf Atlas alone says the frequent winter NW winds are generally offshore (315), which agrees. Stormrider's J-Bay page (stormrider.surf/break/j-bay) says 'SW-W is offshore for most of the sections, while NW-NE Berg (or Devil) winds descend from the mountains, blowing into the barrels', with wind 'South Westerly'. That text is only in the page's script data, which the excerpt checker cannot see, so it was not recorded; it contradicts Surf Atlas's NW. Most readable evidence centres the offshore on about 225-250 deg, not 290. Swell direction: SSW/SW from WSL, Surf-Forecast, Surf Atlas, WannaSurf and Stormrider (region). Yeeew's S/SE is the outlier and looks templated. Size: WSL 5-15 ft faces matches the profile. Wikipedia's 8-20 ft faces and Yeeew's 3-18 ft (my conversion) run higher; WannaSurf says best at 4-8 ft. Period: only WSL gives a number (12 s+), equal to the profile minimum. Tide: WSL (low to mid best, works all tides) and Yeeew (all) agree with 'all'; WannaSurf says mid. Seasonality: winter / May-August from Surf Atlas and Stormrider (region), and summer flat from Surf-Forecast. All agree with May-September. The Stormrider claims come from its St Francis Bay region page and are region-level.

keramas.notes: Wind: a NW-quadrant offshore (profile 320) is supported by Surf-Forecast (NNW), Indonesian Surf Guide (N-W) and Padang Padang Surf Camp's Uluwatu page ('NW monsoon'). The same camp is inconsistent elsewhere. Its Keramas page lists 'E or NE light to moderate' as the wind (not labelled offshore, so no value), and its FAQ says the SW-W monsoon is offshore at east-facing breaks (247.5, contradicting). Both the camp and the FAQ credit a cold morning mountain (Agung) wind as offshore, with no compass direction. So wind support is moderate, with one publisher contradicting itself. Swell direction: S-SSW is well supported (195-205 from the surf camp; SSW from Surf-Forecast; S/SW from WSL and Surfing-Waves; SE-S from Surf Atlas). WSL's 'west' goes beyond the profile window. Size: 3-10 ft from WSL, Surfing-Waves and the surf camp (2-10 ft) matches the profile. Tide conflicts. Mid to high: WannaSurf, WSL, Surfing-Waves; high: Indonesian Surf Guide. Mid only, with high tide rejected: Padang Padang Surf Camp (the FAQ just says mid). Surfing-Waves contradicts itself with 'mid to low'; Surf Atlas says only avoid dead low. Season: the wet season (November/December-March/April) is now from four publishers, consistent with the profile. Period: no numeric working range. The surf camp says 20 s swells arrive smaller than 14 s ones but barrel harder, and Surf Atlas says long periods, qualitatively. Bathymetry: descriptive only (lava/volcanic rock reef, rivermouth sediment bulge, a ridge with channels either side). No measured survey or peer-reviewed study found (Crossref: only social-science papers for Keramas village). The three Padang Padang Surf Camp entries (Keramas page, Uluwatu page remark, FAQ) are one publisher.

kirra.notes: Read directly: Wikipedia (Kirra and Snapper Rocks pages), Surf-Forecast, WannaSurf, City of Gold Coast, National Surfing Reserves, WSL Secrets, Experience Gold Coast, Surf Atlas, TSB 1997 surf impact assessment, TSB Feb 2024 committee notes. GROYNE HISTORY conflicts: Wikipedia says the groyne was built in May 1972, while the 1997 government assessment says it was extended 400 m in 1974. For the 30 m removal, Wikipedia says 1995 and TSB 1997 says June 1996. Surf Atlas claims a 'later extension' of the groyne restored Kirra, which contradicts both. WIND: Surf-Forecast's 'best wind from the south' (180, at the +-45 boundary of the profile's 225) is the only single readable offshore direction; WannaSurf's SE contradicts it. The Surfing Reserves window (SE/S/SW) and TSB 1997's regional statement that winter SW-NW winds are offshore both contain 225. No readable source names SW explicitly for Kirra. SWELL DIRECTION: SE consensus (Surf-Forecast, WannaSurf, Surfing Reserves E/SE). Experience Gold Coast and Surf Atlas say S-SE, extending up to 30 deg south of the profile optimum max of 150, so consider widening the optimum to ~165. SIZE: WannaSurf starts at 5-6 ft and holds 8 ft+. TSB 1997 gives 1-3 m (pre-1974 classic ride) and 2-4 m near the surfability limit. The council and Experience Gold Coast say it needs big swells. The profile's 3-12 ft fits the upper end; a 3 ft minimum looks low against WannaSurf's 5 ft. PERIOD: no source. TIDE: WSL's 'solid swell and low tide' supports low_to_mid; Surf-Forecast says tide doesn't matter. SEASON: Surf-Forecast autumn-winter and Surf Atlas winter-and-fall overlap the profile only in Mar-May; Surf Atlas's winter-spring 'sweet spot' contradicts it. The profile's Jan-Feb has no readable support. RECENCY: Kirra's quality has suffered since the Superbank (Wikipedia). TSB notes read but not recorded (Aug 2019, Nov 2019, Feb 2020) mention a dissipated bank, a lagoon and limited surfing. Feb 2024 says Kirra was a fun longboard wave. No measured bathymetry dataset was read.

la-graviere-hossegor.notes: Five readable sources from four publishers (Surf-Forecast, Wikipedia, WSL x2, Ultimate France). Wind: east is stated by three publishers (Surf-Forecast, WSL, Ultimate France), 5 deg from the profile's 95; all are now read directly. Swell direction: W (Surf-Forecast), W-NW (WSL), W and N (Ultimate France) agree with the profile window. Size conflict: WSL head-high to double overhead+ (about 5-12 ft) against Ultimate France 0.5-2.5 m (about 1.6-8.2 ft, 'holds shape up to 2.5 m'); both overlap the profile's 3-15 ft, but neither supports 15 ft. Period conflict: WSL's 9-12 s ideal is below the profile's 14 s ideal; no other source gives a period. Tide conflict: WSL says any tide at La Gravière; Ultimate France says outgoing tide best, incoming tide closes out and high tide is dead. Neither supports the profile's 'mid' directly; Ultimate France at least rules out high tide. Season: autumn (Surf-Forecast, Ultimate France) and autumn-winter for the region (WSL 2022) all agree; nothing specific to February-March. Sand bottom, dated: WSL 2015 (sandbank, offshore trench), WSL 2022 and Ultimate France 2026 (several good sandbanks). No measured bathymetry. Crossref found Capbreton canyon-head morphobathymetry papers (e.g. Marine Geology 2014, 2020), but none names La Gravière, so none was recorded.

lakey-peak.notes: Wind, previously unsupported, now has readable support near the profile's 60 deg: east (Surf Atlas, 'E trade winds coming straight offshore'), northeast (Yeeew), SE to NE (Indonesian Surf Guide, midpoint E) and SE, NE (Lineup); Surf-Forecast's ESE (112.5 deg) stays the outlier. Lineup's text closely mirrors Indonesian Surf Guide and may be derived from it. Tide: all tides (WannaSurf, Indonesian Surf Guide, Yeeew, Lineup), with the left working through the tide and the right needing mid to high tide; Surf-Forecast says high and Kala Surf says mid-high. The profile's 'all' is well supported. Swell direction: SW (Surf-Forecast, Surf Atlas), S-SW (Indonesian Surf Guide), S (Yeeew), inside the profile window. Size: WannaSurf 3-5 ft start, holds 8 ft+; Indonesian Surf Guide and Yeeew waist high to double overhead (about 3-12 ft faces, an approximate conversion), consistent with the profile's 3-10 ft. Period: only 'groundswells more frequent than windswells' (Surf-Forecast); no numbers found. Season: May-October (Surf-Forecast, Surf Atlas), June-September (WannaSurf, Kala), April-October (Lineup), all inside the profile. Wave direction: an A-frame with a left and a right (Indonesian Surf Guide, Surf Atlas, WannaSurf, Surf-Forecast), supporting 'both'; indonesia.travel's 'waves sweep to the left' is about Lakey Beach in general. Kala Surf's wind lines contradict each other, so no wind was recorded from it. Surfer Today still 403. No peer-reviewed, survey or official source found.

lobitos.notes: Wind conflict, now better documented. East as best/offshore: Surf-Forecast (guide text), LatAm Surfing, Real Surf Travel and Surfing-Waves; all 60 deg from the profile's 150. Southeast or ESE: WannaSurf SE, Surf Escape SE, and Surf-Forecast's best-conditions line (ESE); 15-37.5 deg off. Surf-Forecast contradicts itself (ESE pairing vs 'ideal winds from the east'). The profile's 150 has partial support, but more independent sources say E. Swell direction: Surf-Forecast's guide text says NW, while its own best-conditions line and every other source say S/SW. Two sources say NW and N swells are the summer (November-May) swells, and smaller. Tide: WannaSurf (mid and high) and the 2012 blog (mid on the push) support the profile's mid_to_high. Viva Mancora and Surf Escape say all tides. Size: WannaSurf 3 ft to 6 ft+ (open top). The blog says La Punta maxes out above triple overhead (about 18 ft faces), so the profile max of 10 may be low, but evidence is thin. Season: winter (April/May/June to September/October) from six publishers, consistent with the profile's March-October. No numeric period, apart from magicseaweed data that was excluded. Sand-bottom evidence: the La Punta sand banks were affected by beachfront construction (Surfonomics 2020), the wave changes with the sand (WannaSurf), and the 1998 El Niño sediment created the waves (Wikipedia). Lobitos has several breaks (Baterias, El Hueco, Frontera, La Punta, Generales, Piscinas, Los Muelles). Sources do not always say which break their data refer to. WannaSurf's 'Lobitos' listing reads like a hollow reef break near El Hueco, while the guides describe La Punta as a mellow sand-bottom point. Surfonomics is a university/NGO research e-book, not peer-reviewed; it is classed community because no better v1.2 category fits. No peer-reviewed wave or bathymetry study found (Crossref: only social-science and geology papers on Lobitos).

macaronis.notes: Tide: the profile's 'mid' is contradicted. All tides is stated by Surf-Forecast, WannaSurf (falling best), both Macaronis Resort pages, Indonesian Surf Guide and Surf Indonesia, plus Surfer Today (unread); only Surfing-Waves.com says mid tide. Wind: NE (Surf-Forecast, 45 deg), E (Surf Indonesia, 90 deg) and E-SE (Indonesian Surf Guide and Surfing-Waves, 112.5 deg) all lie within 45 deg of the profile's 70; several sources stress that it handles most winds (WannaSurf lists six good directions, the resort says some prefer a light onshore SW breeze). The E-SE values are 42.5 deg off, close to the agreement limit. Swell direction: SW (Surf-Forecast, Surf Indonesia, Resort), S-SW with 200-210 deg best (Resort surf page, slightly south of the profile's 210-245 optimum), SW-W (Indonesian Surf Guide), W-SW-S (WannaSurf). Size: WannaSurf 3-5 ft start, holds 10 ft+; Resort 2-8 ft (3-6 ft ideal); Surfing-Waves 2-8 ft; Indonesian Surf Guide waist high to 1.5x overhead. All are consistent with 3-10 ft, though the resort and Surfing-Waves do not state a scale. Period: no numbers found. Season: May-October (Surf-Forecast), surfable almost daily in the southern winter (Resort), year-round (Surf Indonesia). The two resort pages are one publisher, the break's own resort operator. The Inertia page was dropped (claims not on it). Surfer Today still 403. No peer-reviewed or survey source found.

margaret-river-main-break.notes: Read directly: WSL 2015 breakdown, WSL 2018 event guide (one publisher), Surf-Forecast (identity confirmed as the WA Surfers Point), WannaSurf ('Margaret river left' page), Perth is OK! (2019/2023), Surf Europe. Could not read (403): margaretriver.com x2, SurferToday, surfnerd. A WSL page carrying a Surfline event forecast (posts/499542) was read but not used: it is forecast text. SWELL DIRECTION: SW-WSW (WSL table), WSW (Surf-Forecast), inside the optimum. WIND: east (WSL table, Surf-Forecast); WSL's text also says a light SE blows offshore; WannaSurf lists an SE-E-NE window. TIDE: WSL 'Tide: Any' supports the profile's 'all'. PERIOD: mid-long (WSL), groundswell more common (Surf-Forecast); no seconds. SIZE: WSL table 4-15 ft+, WSL guide 2-20 ft, WannaSurf to 16 ft+ (scales not stated). WSL also says the right disappears at about 10 ft and that beyond 12-15 ft 'all bets are off' (closeouts linking with The Box). The profile's 20 ft max rests on the guide's 2-20 ft and the general 'handles about as big as you want'. SEASON: two regional magazine statements (Perth is OK!, Surf Europe) say autumn (Mar-May) is best; Surf-Forecast says all year (not comparable). Nothing supports the profile's Jun and Sep-Oct. BATHYMETRY: a deep-water reef with the shallow Surgeon's Table ledge (WSL); WannaSurf says reef with sharp rocks. No survey or peer-reviewed study was found (Crossref searches returned nothing relevant).

mavericks.notes: All 5 readable current sources were re-read and 2 new ones added: WannaSurf and SFBayWeather. WIND: E offshore from Surf-Forecast and WannaSurf (readable), plus Surfertoday (403). SWELL DIRECTION: Surf-Forecast WNW fits the 280-305 optimum. WannaSurf NW and SFBayWeather 300-315 lean further north, while NOAA 2007 says the usual NW waves are too small and the breaking winter waves come from 'more westerly directions'. Treat the optimum's northern edge as uncertain. SIZE CONFLICT: Wikipedia (tops out over 60 ft), Visit Half Moon Bay (up to 60 ft) and SFBayWeather (40-60 ft faces regularly) all exceed the profile max of 50. PERIOD: first numeric support is SFBayWeather (18-20+ s for larger faces), a community-grade source. TIDE CONFLICT persists: WannaSurf all tides (readable) and Surfertoday all tides (403) contradict the profile's 'mid', and no source supports mid. SEASON: Nov-Mar (Visit HMB, SFBayWeather) and winter (USGS, NOAA, Surf-Forecast, Wikipedia). BATHYMETRY is the best documented of the batch: USGS OFR 2014-1214 (Purisima Formation bedrock reef) and the NOAA 2007 multibeam survey. Consistency: Visit HMB says only a few ideal days even in a good winter, which conflicts with Surf-Forecast's 'consistent'. Not readable (403): Surfertoday, SURFER, californiabeaches.com. Visit Half Moon Bay was reclassified official -> magazine (tourism board).

mullaghmore-head.notes: 11 sources: 10 read directly, plus SurferToday kept as web_search (403). 10 publishers. WIND remains weak and disputed. WannaSurf lists SE/E/NE as good wind (centred on E, 45 deg from 135). Surf Holidays says it works best with southwesterly winds (contradicts by 90 deg). RTE (2025) reports the usual westerly winds are too dangerous and that the wind switching southwest produced spectacular waves (an observation, so no value). No readable source explicitly confirms SE. The SE/S-SW statements on Surf-Forecast and Surf Atlas are about Mullaghmore Beach, not the Head, and were excluded. Swell direction: WannaSurf NW and W, Surf Holidays W to NW. Both overlap 285-320. Size: Surf Holidays 'starts breaking at about 10ft and can hold waves of up to 50ft and beyond', which matches the profile's 10-50 exactly (the profile may derive from it). WannaSurf says it starts at 12 ft+ and holds 16 ft and over (WannaSurf's top bin). Surf Atlas says it comes into its own over 15 ft swell and is best around 30-40 ft. Surfing-Waves says it easily holds over 20 ft. Record-day heights (49 ft in 2012 on Wikipedia, 60 ft from SurferToday) are not working ranges; SurferToday's unchanged 60 ft claim should not set the max. Tide: Surf Holidays high (it needs high tide to break out from the rock), WannaSurf mid and high, SurferToday (unread) high only. Consistent with mid_to_high, leaning high. Season: Surf Holidays late autumn and winter (Nov-Feb), Surf Atlas Dec-Mar, SurferToday (unread) Oct-Mar. All inside Oct-Mar. Period: no source gives a number, so the 14/17 s profile values are unverified. Bathymetry: GSI (official, 2004) describes the Head as a rock platform of Carboniferous sandstone, siltstone and shale; this is land and foreshore geology, not a survey of the reef. WannaSurf says flat rocks; Surf Atlas a barnacle-covered rock ledge; Surf Holidays a ledge of reef. Location: about 400-500 m NW/N of the village (Wikipedia, Surf Atlas). No peer-reviewed study of the break was found on Crossref.

mundaka.notes: Eight sources from eight publishers, six read directly (ScienceDirect and Surfertoday are 403 and kept from the search pass). The page gives 2004 and 230,000 m3 for the dredging, ScienceDirect's summary 2003, and Save The Waves 243,000 m3. Swell direction (NW) agrees everywhere it is stated, but Breakfinder's templated line says NNE. Wind: S (Surf-Forecast), S-SW (Surf Atlas intro, Breakfinder, Surfertoday) agree with the profile's 180; Surf Atlas's spot section says SE, a conflict within that page (recorded at the 45-deg edge). Tide: low (Surf-Forecast, Surf Atlas) to low-mid (Breakfinder, Surfertoday) all overlap the profile's low to mid; a rising tide after low is preferred by Surf Atlas, a falling one by Surf-Forecast. Season: autumn peak (Surf Atlas), winter over 50% surfable (Wikipedia), September-December (Surfertoday); February-March is supported only by Surf Atlas's 'can be in winter or spring'. Sand bottom, dated: dredging in 2003-2004 destroyed the sandbar, and the 2005 contest was cancelled; it began to recover in 2006 (Save The Waves 2008; Wikipedia; npj Ocean Sustainability 2023). No measured surf-zone bathymetry was found. Ride length conflict: 200 m (Surf Atlas) vs 400 m (Save The Waves, Breakfinder). Frequency: 50-70 days a year (Surf Atlas), about 50 (Surfertoday), one day in three 'perfect' (Wikipedia). Breakfinder caution: its header calls Mundaka an A-frame beach break; only its descriptive paragraphs were used. Save The Waves is an NGO-commissioned economic study (community). The npj piece is a short journal comment. Gaps: no swell period figure (only 'groundswell'); size numbers only from Surfertoday (not re-readable, 403).

nazare.notes: Six readable sources from four publishers (Wikipedia x2, Surf-Forecast x2, Research, Society and Development, nazarewaves.com). Wind: Surf-Forecast says east (both pages), matching the profile's 90; nazarewaves.com says NE ideally or N, which is 45 deg off (edge of agreement), so the evidence points to E to NE rather than exactly E. Swell direction: W (Surf-Forecast) and NW (nazarewaves) bracket the profile's 280-310 optimum; no source gives degrees. Period: two sources give 14 s or more as the threshold for the canyon effect (profile minimum 13 s, ideal 17 s). They are not independent: the 2022 paper and nazarewaves.com list the same three conditions (14 s or more, over 4 m, about 3x amplification), so one probably drew on the other. The RSD journal is an open-access Brazilian journal with fast review (received 08/06, accepted 08/25/2022); treat it as weak peer review. Size: no source gives a working range in breaking-face feet. The '4 m' threshold is the offshore or forecast wave height for the area, not a face height, so it was not recorded; the 15 m and 24-28 m figures are storm or record waves. Bottom type conflict: Surf-Forecast's Praia do Norte page says reef; its Nazare page and Wikipedia say beach. Tide: only Surf-Forecast (all tides); the profile has no preference. Gaps: no official source. The Instituto Hidrográfico page that nazarewaves.com cites is 404. Crossref searches found no surf-break wave-focusing study of Praia do Norte with a readable abstract other than the RSD paper; the ResearchGate study mentioned in the earlier notes (275-315 deg focusing) was not found.

north-point-gracetown.notes: Five readable sources from five publishers: Surf-Forecast, Wikipedia, WannaSurf, Surf Atlas and Swellnet. Stormrider's Southwest Coast region page was read but does not mention North Point, and the Wikipedia Capes surfing-locations list gives only its location; neither was recorded. No peer-reviewed, official or survey source was found. Crossref returned nothing for Gracetown, Cowaramup Bay or Margaret River surf breaks. The Ngari Capes Marine Park documents cited by Wikipedia (fish.wa.gov.au FAQ, UWA PDF) and margaretriver.com did not respond, and the Busselton Mail and Yahoo articles are gone (404). Wind: Surf-Forecast ENE (67.5) and WannaSurf SE/E (112.5) both agree with the profile's 80. A Swellnet contest forecast (2018) says S/SE and SSE winds favour North Point, which suggests the usable wind range reaches further south than 80. It does not use the words offshore or best, so it has no value. Stormrider Surf Guides' North Point page (stormrider.surf/break/north-point-1) holds 'Easterly' wind, 4-15 ft, S-W swell and mid-to-high tide. That matches the profile exactly, so the profile may come from it. Those values are only in the page's script data, which the excerpt checker cannot see, so they were not recorded. Swell direction: SW everywhere (Surf-Forecast, Surf Atlas). WannaSurf's template also lists NW and W. Size: WannaSurf's template minimum (6-8 ft, with 'Dont bother unless everywhere else is big') is above the profile's 4 ft. Surf Atlas says it holds double to triple overhead (about 12-18 ft faces, my conversion), near the profile's 15 ft. Period: no source gives a number; Surf-Forecast says groundswell. Tide: only WannaSurf (mid to high, agrees). Seasonality conflict: Surf-Forecast and Surf Atlas both point to winter. The profile's best months (Mar-Jun, Sep-Oct) share only June with winter. WannaSurf and Surf-Forecast are undated; Wikipedia is 2026, Surf Atlas 2024 and Swellnet 2018.

ocean-beach-sf.notes: Re-read 8 of 11 sources directly; surfertoday.com, surfer.com and sciencedirect.com returned 403 and are kept unchanged as web_search. New readable sources: Journal of Coastal Research abstract (BioOne, 2012) and an Unofficial Networks surf check (2011, east wind offshore and ideal; NW-SW swells). Wind is now supported by two readable sources (surf-forecast.com and Unofficial Networks), both east = 90 deg, matching the profile. Direction: surf-forecast says west (270) and Unofficial Networks NW-SW (225-315), both consistent with the 255-295 optimum. The Inertia only says 'north swells' colloquially, so no number was recorded; it also says some mid-summer south swells miss the beach, which questions the 190 deg end of the swell window. Tide: no readable source supports the profile's 'mid'. surf-forecast.com ('Good surf at all stages of the tide') and WannaSurf ('All tides') both say all tides, recorded as contradicting. The Inertia says low tide throws hardest but makes the paddle-out harder (no preference). Size: WannaSurf gives under 3 ft to 12 ft+ and its description says it holds 15 ft+, matching the profile's 3-15 ft. Period: still no source with numbers (surf-forecast only says clean groundswells prevail). Bathymetry is backed by USGS and JCR abstracts (ebb-tidal delta focuses wave energy on the central/southern beach) plus dated 2022 magazine evidence that the bars shift constantly. The surf-forecast page has template glitches: its 'Reviews' block describes 'Porthcawl Point' and it lists Kellys Cove (the north end of Ocean Beach) as a separate break 5 km away. Classification note: the USGS 70158958 entry is a conference paper catalogued by USGS. It is kept as official (government geological survey), as in the earlier pass. The JCR abstract is peer_reviewed. The Stormrider break page for Ocean Beach (/break/ocean-beach) renders its text only with JavaScript, so nothing could be cited from it.

padang-padang.notes: Wind: SE (135, the profile value) is supported by Surf-Forecast, Indonesian Surf Guide, Padang Padang Surf Camp (two pages) and Surfer Today (unread). Surf Atlas says east (90), at the 45 deg limit. Swell direction: SW/SSW broadly agrees. Padang Padang Surf Camp's FAQ gives 210-225, at or just below the profile optimum (215-240). Indonesian Surf Guide says a south swell lines it up better (180, outside the profile window), a real disagreement. Tide is the main conflict. Mid: Surf-Forecast, and WannaSurf text for swells over 5 ft. Low or low-mid: Padang Padang Surf Camp (both pages), Surf Atlas, and WannaSurf for swells over 8 ft. High: Indonesian Surf Guide, which stresses safety rather than quality. All: WannaSurf's template field. The profile's 'mid' has two direct supports against four low/low-mid statements, so it is weakly supported. Size: WannaSurf (3-12 ft field; the 'real Padang' at 6-12 ft text) and Indonesian Surf Guide (head high to double overhead, about 6-12 ft faces) fit the profile max of 12. The local surf camp says it is best at double to triple overhead (about 12-18 ft faces) and sections below that, which points to a higher range than the profile's 4-12. Period: the only number is 'regularly exceeding 16 s' for the peak-season swells (Padang Padang Surf Camp), consistent with the profile's 13 s min and 17 s ideal. Season: May-September/October across five publishers; the camp says June-August is most consistent. No peer-reviewed wave study found. Crossref found only architecture, tourism and cliff-stability papers for Padang Padang.

WIND: E (Surf-Forecast, 90), NE (MyWaveFinder, 45), N/NE (Surf Holidays, about 22.5) and NE-E (surftrips, about 67.5). Everything falls within 45 deg of the profile's 50, and the centre of the evidence is close to NE-ENE. SWELL DIRECTION: S to SW throughout (S, SSW, SW), consistent with the profile. TIDE CONFLICT, unresolved: low or low-rising (Surf-Forecast, MyWaveFinder), all tides (Surf Holidays, Surfertoday), mid-to-high (Costa Rica Surf Company), size-dependent (surftrips: higher water on small days, low on big days). Only one source matches the profile's mid. SIZE: surftrips gives 4-12 ft (its own field says 2-12 ft); Surfertoday (search-only) gives best 4-8 ft. MyWaveFinder's monthly 'swell height' row is a climatology, not a working range, so it was not recorded. PERIOD: no numbers anywhere; only 'groundswells more frequent than windswells'. SEASON: April-October (MyWaveFinder), March-October (Surf Holidays, surftrips), May-November (Costa Rica Surf Company) and April-August (Surfertoday). The profile's April-September is inside all of these; several also extend to October. surftrips.co says it is cross-checked against Surfline/Stormrider/WannaSurf (derivative). MyWaveFinder, Surf Holidays and Costa Rica Surf Company are commercial travel/brand pages (community).

pipeline.notes: All 5 readable current sources were re-read and 4 new readable sources added: WSL 2022 Essentials, hawaii.surf, WannaSurf fields and Caldwell 2005 (JCR). WIND is now well supported from 4 readable publishers: Surf-Forecast (SE on the Pipeline listing, ESE on the Pipeline and Backdoor listing), WSL (calm or light SE), hawaii.surf (S-SE) and WannaSurf (S). All are within 45 deg of the profile's 135. SWELL DIRECTION: Surf-Forecast WNW/NW, WSL W-NW (Lopez: any NW, a slight west angle gives hollower waves), hawaii.surf 295-340 and WannaSurf NW-W all fit. Wikipedia instead says a W swell clears sand and a N swell then gives the best waves, so N (A-frame and Backdoor) is recorded as contradicting the 295-320 optimum. SIZE: hawaii.surf 6-15 ft faces, WSL a few feet overhead to triple overhead (about 8-18 ft, converted from overhead), WannaSurf from 3 ft, and Wikipedia up to about 20 ft. The profile's 4-15 is broadly right, but the top may be low. PERIOD: the first numeric support is hawaii.surf (16+ s for classic Pipe, 10-14 s favours Backdoor), a single community source. TIDE: Surf-Forecast (B&B listing) says all stages. hawaii.surf says it works most tides but is best on low-mid, recorded as a mild contradiction. SEASON: hawaii.surf Nov-Mar, Caldwell 2005 Oct-Mar high-surf season (region-wide, not spot-specific), Surf-Forecast summer-flat. REEF: Wikipedia, WannaSurf and hawaii.surf say flat lava/tabletop reef. The Surfertoday limestone claim (403, unchanged) remains a conflict. WannaSurf's own type field says 'Reef-coral' while its text says lava. Not readable (403): Surfertoday x2, SURFER, GoHawaii (reclassified official -> magazine per methodology v1.2; claims unchanged). The EOS Pipeline entry is paywalled. No Pipeline-specific peer-reviewed or measured bathymetry was found.

playa-hermosa-cr.notes: Nine sources from eight publishers; seven were read, and the two Surfertoday pages are kept as search-only. Dated sources for this sand-bottom break: Wikipedia 2026, Wikivoyage 2026, Surf Atlas 2024, WSL 2022, Surfer Factory 2021. SWELL DIRECTION CONFLICT, now clearer: Surf-Forecast says W (270, outside the profile window). Backyard Hotel gives SW/W for the main peak, and Surfertoday (search-only) SW/W. Surf Atlas gives S-SW, and Surfer Factory gives S/SW for Almendro. Peaks along the 10-12 km beach differ (the Backyard Hotel page lists W for Tulin and Roca Loca). The profile's optimal 190-230 is supported by Surf Atlas and the Almendro entries. Surf-Forecast's 'west' and the hotel's SW/W suggest extending the optimal window towards 250-260. WIND: NE offshore (Surf-Forecast, Surfertoday) and 'easterly offshores' (Surf Atlas), consistent with the profile's 50. TIDE: mid-to-high is supported for the main peaks (Backyard Hotel, Surf Atlas Almendros, Surfer Factory Almendro), matching the profile. Some peaks (Terraza, Tulin) prefer lower tides. SIZE CONFLICT: Surf Atlas gives ideal 5-9 ft with closeouts above 12 ft at Almendros. Backyard Hotel says the beach tends to close out at about 8 ft+. The profile maximum of 12 ft may be high for the beach itself. PERIOD: no numbers; only 'mostly groundswells'. SEASON: wet season May-October (Surf Atlas) and April-November (Surfertoday, search-only), consistent with the profile's April-October. Several sources stress year-round consistency. The Surf-Forecast guide places it in 'Golfo de Nicoya', but its nearest airports (Quepos 54 km, SJO 64 km) match the Jaco-area Playa Hermosa, not the Guanacaste one.

Visit Mexico's source_type was changed to magazine, because tourism boards are not official under v1.2, and WSL pages are now magazine too. New readable sources: The Inertia (2018) and Surf Atlas (2025). Wind remains the weak variable. Only surf-forecast.com gives a direction: NE (45), matching the profile's 40, after correcting the earlier NNE. The Inertia, WannaSurf and Surf Atlas agree mornings are offshore until about 10-11 am, but give no direction. WannaSurf's 'Good wind direction: SouthWest' would be onshore at this south-facing beach and looks like a data error. Direction is strongly supported: WSL 180-225, surf-forecast SSW, WannaSurf SW, Surf Atlas S. WSL's 163-280 window is close to the profile's 150-260; the WSL piece was written with Surfline forecasters' help. Size: WannaSurf gives 3-5 ft to 16 ft+ and WSL a 20-25 ft contest day. The Inertia says it handles 30 ft peaks, above the profile's 25 ft maximum. Wikipedia's 'up to sixteen metres' is a record figure and was not recorded. Tide: still no source (the profile says mid). Period: no readable number. WSL's '15 seconds apart... 25 seconds apart' is general swell physics, not a Puerto preference, so it was not recorded. Bathymetry conflict: most sources describe sandbars over an offshore canyon/trench (WSL, Stormrider, The Inertia), while WannaSurf lists reef with sand. Season: all readable sources fall within April-October, inside or near the profile's April-September.

punta-de-lobos.notes: Re-read 4 of 5 current sources; surfertoday.com returned 403 and is kept unchanged. New readable sources: Surf Atlas Pichilemu (2026), Wavelength (2024) and GoChile (2010, Spanish). Wind remains thin. Only surf-forecast.com gives an offshore direction: ESE (112), within about 23 deg of the profile's 135. WannaSurf lists an S/SE/E wind window and says north winds blow it out, and Wavelength says the cliffs shelter it from the almost daily SW wind. Neither states an offshore direction. Direction: SW (225) from surf-forecast.com and Surf Atlas fits the 210-240 optimum. WannaSurf's N-S list is too broad. Season: Surf Atlas (March-October) matches the profile exactly; surf-forecast.com (winter) and the WSL tour window (April-August) sit inside it. Tide conflict: WannaSurf says low and mid are best, against the profile's 'all'. No other source gives a tide. Size is the main open question. The working ranges are WannaSurf under 3 ft to 16 ft+, Surf Atlas head-high to 25 ft, Wavelength 3-30 ft, WSL 'holds as big as it gets', and GoChile 'from 2 m up'. None confirms the profile's 40 ft maximum, although Wavelength reports 50 ft faces at a 2022 event (a record figure, not recorded). GoChile's 2 m minimum conflicts with WannaSurf and Wavelength (3 ft). Period: only a qualitative 'long-period' (Surf Atlas). No peer-reviewed or official source was found; Crossref returned none, and the Pichilemu municipal culture plan noted in the earlier pass is not in the current source list, so it could not be re-read. The Suston and Carve pages only cover the World Surfing Reserve and were not recorded. A Meteored (2026) article covers Pichilemu generally, citing Chile.Travel, and was not recorded.

punta-roca.notes: Eight readable sources from six publishers (Surf-Forecast, Wikipedia, WSL x3, El Salvador Travel, surftrips.co, Surfsphere). WIND: support for a N to NNE offshore: Surf-Forecast NNE, surftrips N, Surfsphere N/NE. The profile's 20 deg fits. CAUTION: a WSL-hosted 2022 forecast post calls NE a sideshore 'devil wind'. Search summaries of Surfer's 'Surf Spot Mechanics' (403, not readable) reportedly say NW is the best offshore and NE is unfavorable sideshore. If confirmed, the profile's 20 deg may be too far east. TIDE CONFLICT: 'all tides' (Wikipedia, El Salvador Travel, surftrips) against mid-to-high (WSL forecast post) and low-to-mid (Surfsphere). Wikipedia says low gives more barrels; WSL says low runs smaller; surftrips says low exposes the boulders. The profile's 'mid' sits between them, and no source names mid alone. SIZE: El Salvador Travel gives best 4-8 ft, up to 12 ft; surftrips gives 3-12 ft (it says it is cross-checked against Surfline, Stormrider and WannaSurf, so it is not independent). Wikipedia's good-day 6-8 ft Hawaiian (about 12-16 ft faces) is bigger than both. SEASON: surftrips gives April-October (matches the profile). El Salvador Travel says rideable year-round, most epic March-April. PERIOD: only 'clean groundswells prevail' (Surf-Forecast); no numbers. The 2022 WSL post is Surfline-authored forecast copy hosted on worldsurfleague.com. Only its general tide and wind characterisations were recorded, never forecast numbers. Drop it if Surfline-authored text should be excluded entirely.

raglan-manu-bay.notes: 9 sources, all read directly. 8 publishers (WSL counted once). TIDE CONFLICT, which the profile should resolve. Surf-Forecast says best around low tide. WannaSurf says low and mid. Surf Girl NZ, Surfara and MyWaveFinder say all tides, adding that low tide is hollower and faster and high tide mellower or chunkier. Only Strike Mission's model profile says mid. Several sources agree the wave is more hollow at low tide. Consider changing the profile from 'mid' to 'low_to_mid' or 'all'. SWELL DIRECTION: Surf-Forecast, Surf Girl NZ, Surfara and MyWaveFinder all say SW (225), inside the 220-260 optimum; Strike Mission's profile is WSW 210-280. WannaSurf's NW/W is the outlier (it may describe the swell window rather than the best direction). WIND: SE (135) from Surf-Forecast (offshore), Surf Girl NZ and Surfara; WannaSurf SW/S/SE. All agree with 140. MyWaveFinder says E and Strike Mission's profile says E (90, offshore range 50-130); both are 50 deg off and marked as contradicting. Surf-Forecast notes waves can be OK in light onshore winds. Size: Wikipedia 2-10 ft+, WannaSurf 3-16 ft+, WSL best contest day 4-5 ft. These overlap the profile's 3-12. Period: no source gives a number apart from Strike Mission's 14 s reference (model input). Surf-Forecast and Surfara say mostly groundswell. The 11/15 s profile values are otherwise unsupported. Season: WSL scheduled the 2026 CT for May 15-25, 'the optimal time of year'. MyWaveFinder says Mar-Jun (Raglan generally) and Strike Mission Mar-Oct. All are inside the profile's Mar-Oct. Strike Mission matches the profile's season and swell window almost exactly, which is a circularity warning: treat it as another app's assumptions. Independence: Surf Girl NZ and MyWaveFinder share near-identical text, and Surfara and MyWaveFinder share the sentence 'rocky point break is consistently fed by south westerly ground swells throughout the year'. These three community sources are probably one origin. Bathymetry: WannaSurf says a boulder bottom with a hard reef 'ledge' section toward Whale Bay; no survey or readable peer-reviewed bathymetry. The Scarfe et al. 2009 JCR abstract and the 1996 Waikato District Council reserve plan (scanned PDF) could not be read.

restaurants.notes: Seven publishers, all read directly. Tide is still the main conflict. Yeeew is the only source that directly supports the profile's mid_to_high ('Works on a mid to high tide best'; the reef is 'best avoided at low'). Against it: WSL (Mid or Mid-low), Tourism Fiji ('All, but best at low'), WannaSurf (all tides, rising) and the Tavarua resort (all tides, skill-dependent). Tourism Fiji also notes that higher tides make it less scary. Wind is well supported: SE (Yeeew), SE/E (WannaSurf) and ESE trades offshore (Perfect Wave Travel), all within 15 deg of the profile's 120. WSL's table line 'Light S to SSE 5-10kts or light/variable' is not called offshore or best and includes light/variable, so it is recorded with no offshore value. It no longer counts against the profile. Size disagrees at the top end. WSL (3-6 ft) and the Tavarua resort (2-6 ft) give maximums well below the profile's 10 ft. WannaSurf (3-10 ft+) and Yeeew (waist high to double overhead) agree with it. The 6 ft figures may be back-measured local sizes, so this may be a scale difference rather than a real conflict. Seasonality gap filled: Perfect Wave Travel says the swells Restaurants needs are rare from November to April, which matches a May-October season. The profile also includes April. Period: WSL's 11-15 s is still the only number. Bathymetry is qualitative only (shallow coral reef). No peer-reviewed or survey source mentions Restaurants, and Surf-Forecast has no Restaurants page. The WSL URL without its slug opens the same 2015 post as the Cloudbreak source, and its table covers both breaks.

rifles.notes: Wind is the main conflict, and the readable evidence now mostly contradicts the profile's northeast (45 deg). West to northwest is named as the ideal or best wind by Playground Surf Resort (W to NW), Yeeew (NW), Surf Indonesia (NW) and Botik Resort (NNW). Sumatran Surfariis explains that the wave sits at the SE tip of the island, so any north or east wind over about 5 knots ruins it, and it can be offshore in a west wind. Surf Camp Sumatra and Surfer Today (unread) say it needs, or starts firing with, some west in the wind. Indonesian Surf Guide and surftrips give E-SE instead. Only Surf-Forecast (NE) and WannaSurf (N, E, NE) support 45 deg. Playground's and Surf Camp Sumatra's texts share wording, so they are not independent. The profile's offshore wind should be reviewed; W to NW (about 270-315 deg) has the broadest support. Swell direction: S (Playground, Surf Camp Sumatra, Yeeew, Surf Indonesia, Botik), S-SW (WannaSurf, surftrips 180-225), SSW (Surf-Forecast), consistent with the profile; Indonesian Surf Guide's SW-W is the outlier. Size: 5-12 ft (WannaSurf, surftrips), 4-8 ft (Botik), head high to triple overhead+ (Indonesian Surf Guide) and chest high to triple overhead (Yeeew); the profile's 12 ft maximum matches WannaSurf and surftrips, while its 4 ft minimum is below the 5-6 ft most sources give. Tide: mid to high (WannaSurf, Indonesian Surf Guide, surftrips, Yeeew, Surf Indonesia, Botik) and high (Playground); the profile's mid_to_high is well supported. Period: no numbers found. Season: April-October (Surf Camp Sumatra, surftrips, Surf Indonesia), early season April/May (Playground), May-October (Surf-Forecast). Consistency conflict: Surf-Forecast ('very consistent') and WannaSurf ('Very consistent (150 day/year)') against Indonesian Surf Guide, Playground, Surf Camp Sumatra and Yeeew (3/10). surftrips says it was cross-checked against WannaSurf. No peer-reviewed, survey or official source found.

rincon.notes: Re-read 4 of 6 current sources; surfertoday.com and surfer.com returned 403 and are kept unchanged. New readable sources: USGS image description (official) with the first bathymetry evidence (relict submerged boulder delta 1,500 m offshore refracts waves), Surf Atlas (2024), and Stab (2023, storm debris changed the point). Wind: three readable statements support the profile's 20 deg offshore: surf-forecast.com NE (45), Surf Atlas NE for most of the wave (45), and N-NE at the Cove (22). Surf Atlas says Indicator prefers a more easterly offshore. WannaSurf lists NW as the good wind, which conflicts with all of these (value null). Direction: W-NW is consistent across Wikipedia, surf-forecast.com, WannaSurf and Surf Atlas. Note that surf-forecast.com says WNW in its description but 'a West swell' in its best-conditions line. Tide conflict: Wikipedia (low) and Surf Atlas (low tide barrels) support low_to_mid; surf-forecast.com says all stages. Size: Surf Atlas says it maxes out at 13-15 ft, above the profile's 12 ft. Surfer Today's 4-8 ft and Surfer's 6 ft+ (web_search) remain unverified. Swell period: no number in any readable source. Surf Atlas only says locals wait for when 'the period is just right', and Stab mentions very long period swells as a regional forecast, so neither was recorded. Not recorded: Stormrider Ventura says W swells have the most power county-wide (not Rincon-specific), and an O'Reilly et al. 1999 PDF on Santa Barbara Channel swell sheltering (regional, not Rincon-specific; not read). Bathymetry is a cobble/boulder delta, so it changes after floods (Stab 2023).

safi.notes: Seven readable sources from seven publishers; all are community, forecast-site or magazine grade. No guidebook text could be checked, and no official or peer-reviewed source exists for the break. WIND: four sources name the best or offshore wind: N (Surf-Forecast, WannaSurf, Surfsphere) and NE (Surfing-Waves). N is 45 deg from the profile NE (45), at the edge of tolerance. The Stormrider page's embedded break data (script only, not checkable) gives 'Easterly' wind, 3-15 ft, swell 'SW - N', 'Low tide only' and 'uneven reef & sand'. Its description says it only breaks in big swells at low tide. SWELL DIRECTION: WNW (Surf-Forecast), NW (Surfing-Waves, Yeeew) and W (Tidal Trip), all inside the profile window 270-340. SIZE: WannaSurf 6-8 ft to 16 ft+ and Surfing-Waves 'big swells, holds 12ft+'. Several sources say it needs big swell, so the profile minimum of 4 ft may be low. The Stormrider script data gives a 3 ft minimum. TIDE: low tide is consistent across WannaSurf, World Beach Guide, Surfsphere, Tidal Trip (and the Stormrider script data). The profile has tide null, so this could not be compared; consider setting tide_preference to low. PERIOD: no source gives a swell period. Surf-Forecast only says it gets a mix of groundswells and windswells. SEASON: Yeeew gives October-March, consistent with the profile's November-March; Surf-Forecast says summer is flat. WannaSurf's 'Good swell direction' field is empty on the page. The earlier note about a second WannaSurf page listing S/NE swell was not re-checked (no URL in the evidence). No page gives a content date except Surfsphere (2023).

salsa-brava.notes: Seven sources from seven publishers; six were read, and Surfertoday is kept as search-only. TIDE: first support for the profile's mid_to_high: Strike Mission (mid-high) and Crystal Jungle Villa (high, for reef depth). Surf-Forecast and WannaSurf say all tides. The conflict remains, but the evidence now leans towards higher water on safety grounds. WIND: S offshore is consistent (Surf-Forecast, WannaSurf, Strike Mission 150-225), about 30 deg from the profile's 210. SWELL DIRECTION: NE (Surf-Forecast, Strike Mission), E (WannaSurf), E/NE (Costa Rica Waves). Crystal Jungle Villa says E-SE is best, which contradicts the optimal window. PERIOD: Surf-Forecast says it is usually windswell, consistent with the profile's 8 s minimum. Strike Mission's 14 s+ is a model reference, not an observation. SIZE: WannaSurf 5-6 ft to 16 ft+; Crystal Jungle Villa 2 to 12+ ft. SEASON: December-March across Strike Mission, Crystal Jungle Villa and Surfertoday, and srfer November-April; this matches the profile. WAVE DIRECTION CONFLICT: Crystal Jungle Villa and srfer.com call it a left, while Surf-Forecast, WannaSurf and Costa Rica Waves say right (Costa Rica Waves: both ways, rights longer). Their local_behavior statements were not recorded. srfer.com reports the reef changed after an earthquake. The 1991 Limon earthquake uplifted this coast (Plafker & Ward 1992), but no checkable source ties a measured change to Salsa Brava.

shipstern-bluff.notes: Eight publishers: seven read directly (Wikipedia, Surf-Forecast, The Inertia, WannaSurf, ABC News, The Age, Surf Atlas) and Surfer Today (two 403 pages) kept as web_search. Wind is consistent: N offshore (Surf-Forecast) and NNE (Wikipedia), both within 15 deg of the profile's 10. Swell direction: SSW and SW (Surf-Forecast) and huge SW (WannaSurf) fit the profile's 200-225. Wikipedia's WSW is 22.5 deg past the optimum (agrees false). Tide (profile null): Wikipedia says medium to high; Surf-Forecast says best around high tide. WannaSurf's 'Low tide only' comes from a page that mixes two spots and was not used. The evidence leans to mid_to_high or high. Season: winter or June-August from three publishers. Size is still the weak variable. No readable source gives a face-height working range. Wikipedia says 1 m+ (scale unclear) and Surf Atlas says 1 m+ on the swell charts, best at 2 m+. Neither can be compared with the profile's 8-40 ft. Surf Atlas mentions regular 20-30 ft walls (recorded under bathymetry and shape, not as a range). Surfnerd's 4-25 ft range is behind a 403 and was not used. Period: none. No readable source gives a number, and forecast periods are excluded. Bathymetry is qualitative: a shallow ledge or shelf of sharp rock reef, boulders on the bottom and in front of the face, the steps. No survey or peer-reviewed source exists; Crossref found nothing for Shipstern. Parks Tasmania's linked page did not respond. In the resume pass, the remaining Wikipedia references were checked: the Red Bull page returned no text, the SMH 2005 article mentions Shipstern only in passing, and news.com.au did not respond. Yeeew lists no Tasmanian spots. Several of the sources are news features (ABC 2015, The Age 2006). They are dated but anecdotal and support only bathymetry and shape.

skeleton-bay.notes: Fifteen sources from fourteen publishers; fourteen were read directly. Surfer Today returned 403 (Cloudflare) and is kept unchanged as web_search. No peer-reviewed source could be read. Crossref lists Schoonees, Lenhoff and Raw (1999), 'Preventing Natural Breaching of the Major Sand Spit Protecting the Port of Walvis Bay' (Coastal Engineering 1998, doi 10.1061/9780784404119.109), on the Pelican Point spit. It has no abstract in Crossref, and the ASCE page is behind Cloudflare, so nothing was recorded. WIND CONFLICT REMAINS. NE (45) comes from Surf-Forecast, MyWaveFinder and Desert Tracks. MyWaveFinder gives NE for every Namibian spot, and these three may all trace back to Surf-Forecast's templated value. E (90) comes from Surfer Today (unreadable), and SE-E, ideally SE (135), from Wave Safari. The profile's 100 lies between them. Surf Holidays' 'Wind: South, South-West' is the prevailing wind, not an offshore one. Swell direction: SW, or W-SW, everywhere. South Africa Surf Tours and Surf Holidays favour more west, and Desert Tracks says the big west swells that scour the bank have become less reliable. Period: nobody gives a number; all say a big long-period groundswell, with short-period swell not reaching the bay. Size: Surfer Today 4-8 ft and Yeeew 'up to 8 ft' are below the profile's 12 ft maximum. Yeeew is marked agrees false; Surfer Today's earlier agrees true was kept unchanged because the page cannot be read (rule 2); South Africa Surf Tours gives only a 3 m open-ocean chart threshold. TIDE (the profile has no value): low from Stab (2023) and Yeeew; all from Surf-Forecast, Surfer Today, Wave Safari, MyWaveFinder and Surf Holidays. 'All' is the better-supported value, with a lean to low tide. Seasonality: May-September agrees everywhere. BATHYMETRY RECENCY (sand bottom): dated sources say the bank keeps changing. The Inertia (2023) says the bank was tricky for days. South Africa Surf Tours (2025) says the sand shifts every off-season. Desert Tracks (2026) says the wave has degraded into sections, with about 1 million m3 of sand a year moving along the bay. Surf Holidays says the bank only formed after a late-1970s wind shift. Low-weight sources: Yeeew Mag (clear factual errors), Wave Safari (template fields contradict its own text) and MyWaveFinder (templated).

snapper-rocks-superbank.notes: Read directly: Wikipedia, Surf-Forecast, WSL (Secrets 2017/2021; Superbank breakdown 2016), City of Gold Coast, WannaSurf (Snapper and Superbanks pages, one publisher), National Surfing Reserves (2012), Experience Gold Coast (2024), Surf Atlas (Snapper and Kirra pages, one publisher), Tweed Sand Bypassing (1997 surf impact assessment for the NSW/Qld governments; May 2025 advisory committee notes). Could not read (HTTP 403 bot protection): SurferToday x2, ScienceDirect (Crossref has no abstract), ResearchGate; kept as search evidence. WIND is still in conflict. Single-direction statements: Surf-Forecast SE (135, contradicts), WSL light SW (225, supports), Surf Atlas 'SW or W' (247.5, just outside +-45 of 200). Windows: WannaSurf's Snapper page (SW-S-SE) and the Surfing Reserves page (SE/S/SW) both contain the profile's 200; WannaSurf's Superbanks page (NW-W-SW) does not. Surf Atlas says the exposed take-off can suffer more on southerly winds. Read together, S-SW is the best-supported offshore, and Surf-Forecast's SE is the outlier. SWELL DIRECTION is in consensus at E-SE (Surf-Forecast E, WSL ESE, council SE, WannaSurf SE, Surfing Reserves E/SE, Surf Atlas E/SE, TSB 1997 SE/E), inside the optimum. The council page also says 'southerly swell' (same page as 'dominant southeast swell'), and WSL says too-south swells wrap wide while E/NE swells compress. SIZE: WannaSurf below 3 ft to 10 ft+; WannaSurf Superbanks 3-5 to 8 ft+; Experience Gold Coast waist-high to double overhead (~3-12 ft faces); WSL contests from 2 ft. The profile's 2-10 ft is supported. PERIOD: no source gives seconds. WSL says mid-period, and Surf-Forecast says windswell is as likely as groundswell. The 1997 TSB report's regional 'predominant wave period 8 to 12 s, 14 s occurs' is climatology, so it was not recorded as a preference. TIDE: Surf-Forecast and WannaSurf say all tides; only SurferToday (unreadable) says mid-to-low, so the profile's low_to_mid has no readable support. SEASON: Surf-Forecast's autumn-winter supports the profile; Surf Atlas's Jun-Aug contradicts it. BATHYMETRY / RECENCY: the bypass start date conflicts: 1995 (Wikipedia, WSL Secrets; the 1995-96 Stage 1 dredging per TSB 1997) versus 2001 (WSL breakdown, Surf Atlas; the permanent bypass). WSL clarifies that the point's spine is volcanic rock. The newest dated evidence (TSB, May 2025) says TC Alfred (March 2025) eroded Snapper and the bank was only returning by May 2025. No measured bathymetry dataset was read. TSB 1997 used Gold Coast council profiles from 1960-1996, before the Superbank. queensland.com renders its text client-side and could not be checked; not used.

Wikipedia calls the trades offshore without giving a direction (value null). SWELL DIRECTION: NW is consistent across Surf-Forecast, WSL and hawaii.surf (310-340, ideal 315-320). SIZE CONFLICT: WSL 6-18 ft and WannaSurf from 3 ft (proper from 6 ft) fit the profile's 5-18, but hawaii.surf says faces over 25 ft are handled (plus the 403 SURFER, Surfertoday and GoHawaii claims of 20-30 ft), so the profile max of 18 looks low for the outer reef. TIDE: WannaSurf all tides supports 'all'. hawaii.surf is section-dependent (low-mid for the Bowl, mid-high for the Point), so it was not recorded. supertubos.notes: Twelve readable sources from ten publishers: Surf-Forecast, Wikipedia (Portuguese), WSL (three posts), WannaSurf, Surfing-Waves, Yeeew, Surf Atlas, Center of Portugal, The Indian Face and BreakFinder. No peer-reviewed or official study of Supertubos was found. Crossref has only sociology and tourism papers on Peniche; one WebSearch for a bathymetry or morphodynamics thesis found nothing. Not readable: penichesurfguide.com (no response) and visitportugal.com (bot-protection page). TIDE CONFLICT (the profile says low_to_mid): mid to high from WSL's 2015 table and WannaSurf; all tides from Center of Portugal. Mid is best for Yeeew ('all tides, but mid usually is best') and BreakFinder; both agree. No source says low tide is best. A profile value of 'mid' (or mid_to_high) would fit the readable evidence better than low_to_mid. Wind: N-NE agrees with the profile's 40. Surf-Forecast and Yeeew give NE; WSL's text and von Rupp give N; Surfing-Waves N/NE/NW; BreakFinder's text N/NE; pt.wikipedia 'works well with north wind'. N/NW (WannaSurf, The Indian Face) and BreakFinder's templated E contradict. Swell direction: SW-W, with WNW from von Rupp and W/NW from BreakFinder. Everything falls within the window. Size: WSL head high to double overhead (6-12 ft), Center of Portugal up to 12 ft and WannaSurf's minimum 3 ft agree. Yeeew's triple overhead top (about 18 ft) is higher. Period: only von Rupp gives a number, an ideal of about 15 s. Seasonality: the profile's autumn-winter season is supported by WSL (fall into winter) and, indirectly, by Surf-Forecast and WannaSurf (summer flat or poor) and Surf Atlas (tame in August, roaring in December). Bathymetry: sandbars that shift (BreakFinder) but are 'reliable' (von Rupp), with offshore canyon and seafloor relief refracting swell (WSL, von Rupp). Dated sources for this sand-bottom break: Surf Atlas 2026, Yeeew 2024, Center of Portugal 2024, WSL 2015-2019. Low-weight sources: The Indian Face (brand blog), and BreakFinder, whose imported summary line contradicts its own text.

teahupoo.notes: Nine sources from nine publishers; eight were read directly. Surfer Today (403) is kept as web_search. The biggest change: the WSL 'What Makes Teahupo'o Tick' post is Surfline-sourced and was dropped. It was the only source with a 180-220 window, a 14-18 s period and the N/E/ESE wind. Two directly readable spot guides were added by following site indexes: Yeeew and WannaSurf. Wind: Yeeew says the ideal wind is NE (45). Surf-Forecast says NNE (22.5). Surfer Today (search evidence) says a northerly breeze keeps it glassy. All three support the profile's 30. WSL's 2015 best-conditions table says East (60 deg off) and is the only contradiction. The Conversation and Swellnet say the trade winds keep the face clean but name no direction. WannaSurf's wind field is empty. Swell direction: S (Surf-Forecast), S-SW (WSL, Surf Atlas, Yeeew), SW prevailing (Swellnet) and SSW (Surfer Today), all consistent with 190-225. Tide: all tides (Surf-Forecast, Yeeew, WannaSurf). WSL says mid is preferred but it works on all tides. The Conversation explains why: the tidal range is low. Season: winter (Surf-Forecast), May-October (Surf Atlas), storms March-November (WSL) and April-September (Surfer Today); all consistent. Period: The Conversation (Tom Shand, University of Auckland) gives 14-20 s for the arriving swell. Size: WSL's best-conditions 4-12 ft (scale not stated), WannaSurf's start at 3-5 ft and Yeeew's 'chest high to tow-in size' fit the profile's 4 ft minimum. WannaSurf says it holds 16 ft and over, and Yeeew says it gets good up to tow-in size. No source gives a numeric holding maximum, so the profile's 25 ft maximum is unsupported but not contradicted. Bathymetry is qualitative or semi-quantitative only: 51 cm over the reef (Wikipedia), about 1,000 ft deep less than half a mile out (WSL), a shelf at about 10 m (The Conversation). No survey dataset or peer-reviewed paper was found; Crossref returned nothing for Teahupo'o. The Wikipedia shape sentence ('races along into a dry reef closeout') cites Surfline's Surfing A-Z. It was kept because it is Wikipedia text with no conditions data, but it is flagged here. Republications of the Conversation article (Inverse, Swellnet, Daily Maverick and others) were not added as separate publishers.
