thurso-east.notes: 8 sources: 7 read directly, plus SurferToday kept as web_search (403). 7 publishers. Swell direction: Surf-Forecast NNW (337.5); Surf Atlas 'north swell is a must, add some west'; Matosurf N to NW. All fit the 300-345 optimum and 280-30 window. Wind: Surf-Forecast SE (135, offshore), Surf Atlas offshore S or SW (202.5), Matosurf southerly offshore (180). SurferToday (unread) gives S and SE. The profile's 170 is within 35 deg of all of them; together they span SE to SW, centred near S. Tide: Surf-Forecast mid and rising, Surf Atlas mid (too much water fattens it), Matosurf incoming to mid. SurferToday (unread) says medium to high. 'mid' is well supported. Size: Wikipedia 2-15 ft, and North Coast Watersports and Matosurf 'up to 15 ft', which supports the 15 ft max. The 3 ft min is close to Wikipedia's 2 ft. Matosurf's text largely repeats North Coast Watersports and Wikipedia, so the 15 ft figure has about two independent origins. Period: no numbers; Surf-Forecast says mostly groundswell. The 11/15 s profile values are unsupported. Season: Matosurf Oct-Mar, Surf Atlas 'much more common in the winter months' (encoded Dec-Feb), SurferToday (unread) Sep-May. All are inside or overlap the profile's Sep-Apr. Bathymetry: flat layers of Caithness flagstone (Wikipedia, Matosurf); Surf Atlas says slate shelf; World Beach Guide says a shallow, flat, kelp-covered reef. No survey data. Classification conflict: Surf-Forecast calls it a point break, while Wikipedia, Matosurf and World Beach Guide call it a reef. trestles.notes: Re-read 4 of 7 current sources (surf-forecast.com, WannaSurf and two WSL posts). surfertoday.com and surfer.com returned 403. The Stormrider break page returns 200, but its guide text is only in a JavaScript data payload, so it cannot be verified with check_excerpt. That payload reads: 'An often stellar cobblestone peak, Lowers provides occasional hollow, zippering lefts, but is more known for its long, fast, bowling rights. Best with SW swells up to double-overhead. Can be good at any tide.' It is kept as web_search, unchanged. New readable sources: Stab (2016, Tanner Gudauskas) and Pacific Surf School's blog (2025, community). Wind: surf-forecast.com (NE = 45 deg, matches the profile) is the only readable source giving an offshore direction. WannaSurf lists an SE/E/NE wind window, WSL/Biolos says any light wind except south, and Pacific Surf mentions morning offshores, all with value null. Tide conflict: WannaSurf (mid) and WSL/Biolos (mid to incoming) support the profile's mid, but surf-forecast.com says tide does not affect quality. Stormrider (unverifiable payload) also says any tide. Size: WSL gives a head-high to overhead sweet spot (about 5-8 ft) and says it handles virtually any size. WannaSurf says it holds 12 ft+, above the profile's 10 ft maximum, and Stormrider's payload says 'up to double-overhead' (roughly 10-12 ft faces), so the 10 ft maximum looks conservative. Direction: the profile's 180-215 optimum is supported by WSL/Biolos (S) and surf-forecast.com and Pacific Surf (SW 225, 10 deg outside the optimum). Biolos warns that SE hurricane swells are bad, which questions the 150 deg end of the window. Season: surf-forecast.com (summer) and Pacific Surf (April-October) fit the May-October profile. uluwatu.notes: Wind: SE (135) is the dominant answer: Wikipedia, Surf-Forecast, Indonesian Surf Guide (three section pages), and Padang Padang Surf Camp (two pages). All are 15 deg from the profile's 120, so they agree. One contradiction: Surf Atlas gives NE offshores (45 deg) and says wind matters less under the cliffs. Swell direction: SW/SSW across eight publishers, and the numeric values (195-205) sit just below the profile optimum of 205-235. Padang Padang Surf Camp gives an exposure window of about 165-280. Tide is still section-dependent. Mid is supported by Padang Padang Surf Camp (two pages); The Peak is mid-high (Wikipedia, WannaSurf, Indonesian Surf Guide); Racetracks is low; Outside Corner is low or all tides on big swells. Surf-Forecast and WannaSurf's template field say all tides. Size: working ranges of 3-12 ft (WannaSurf, Indonesian Surf Guide's Peak) and 15 ft on big low-tide days (Wikipedia) fit the profile's 3-15. Padang Padang Surf Camp says it holds up to 30 ft, and Wikipedia says Bombie reaches 20 ft (not recorded, a record-style figure). Period: the only numeric value is 14-18 s typical peak-season groundswell (Padang Padang Surf Camp), consistent with the profile's 12 s min and 16 s ideal. Season: April/May-October from five publishers. The peer-reviewed hindcast (J. Marine and Aquatic Sciences, 2018) uses only local wind data, so it describes wind sea (Hs 0.98 m, Ts 5.2 s, from the west), not the groundswell that makes Uluwatu work. Its claims are recorded as not comparable. The excerpts come from its English abstract via Crossref, because ojs.unud.ac.id did not respond. Indonesian Surf Guide and Padang Padang Surf Camp are commercial guide/surf-camp sites (community). Three pages of one publisher (Indonesian Surf Guide) count as one publisher.

waimea-bay.notes: All 5 readable current sources were re-read (the WSL post read over https) and 2 new ones added: hawaii.surf and Caldwell & Aucan 2007 (JCR abstract). WIND (previously only 1 support) now has 3 readable publishers: Surf-Forecast ESE, hawaii.surf SE-S and WannaSurf S, all within 45 deg of 135. SWELL DIRECTION: NW from Surf-Forecast, WannaSurf and hawaii.surf (300-320, range 285-335). WSL shows the size is sensitive to swell direction. SIZE CONFLICT on the minimum: hawaii.surf says the bay doesn't break properly below 15 ft Hawaiian (30 ft faces), and the Eddie needs 30-40 ft faces (Wikipedia) or 40 ft (WSL). WannaSurf's text calls 15 ft a small day, while its template field says 3-5 ft (probably Pinballs and the shorebreak). The profile's 15 ft face minimum may be low for the main bay. Caldwell & Aucan show face height is about 2x the Hawaii scale. PERIOD: first numeric support is hawaii.surf (16+ s), consistent with 14/18. TIDE CONFLICT: hawaii.surf says mid-high is optimal (all workable) and Surfertoday (403) says medium tide, while the profile says all. No readable source says tide does not matter. SEASON: Wikipedia winter, hawaii.surf Nov-Mar (peak Dec-Feb), Caldwell & Aucan fall-spring (region-wide). Not readable (403): Surfertoday, GoHawaii (now magazine), SURFER. No measured bathymetry found. The Pacific Science erosion paper is not about surf.
